# REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE pointer with per-key layering

## Context / Problem
CI and a local developer need different LLM configuration for the same checkout. Today the only
config sources are discovered by walking up from the repo root, so an environment cannot point rebar
at its own file without editing the repo's.

## Approach
Add `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE`, naming a TOML file whose keys LAYER over the discovered config rather
than replacing it. Layering is deliberate: an environment overriding one key must not restate the
whole config, because that duplication is a likelier source of drift than precedence subtlety.
Precedence becomes: CLI `-c llm.KEY` > `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env > REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE > discovered
config file > default.

Prior art for the pointer itself: `KUBECONFIG`, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, `DOCKER_CONFIG` all use an env var
naming a config file. Those REPLACE; rebar layers, for the duplication reason above.

Secondary benefit: hermetic tests. Pointing at an empty file makes model resolution independent of
whatever `rebar.toml` is up-tree — the same trick `AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null` provides for boto3.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` and/or `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — the pointer and its layering.
- `tests/unit/` — precedence tests.

## Testing
Unit tier: config resolution only.
- a key present ONLY in the pointed file is used.
- a key present in BOTH is taken from the pointed file.
- a key present ONLY in the discovered file survives (this is what distinguishes layering from replace).
- env still beats the pointed file.
- a pointer naming a nonexistent file fails loudly rather than silently falling back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts a key set only in the discovered config survives when the pointer supplies other keys
- [ ] a test asserts the pointed file wins per-key over the discovered config
- [ ] a test asserts `REBAR_LLM_<KEY>` env still beats the pointed file
- [ ] a test asserts a pointer to a missing path raises a typed rebar config error naming the variable
- [ ] `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` is read via a string-LITERAL `os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE")`
      call, and `docs/env-vars.md` (regenerated and committed) lists it in the variables table —
      NOT in the "name not statically determinable" section, which is where an indirect read lands
- [ ] re-running `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` after committing produces NO further diff (that
      idempotence is what the CI drift gate actually checks)
- [ ] a test asserts NESTED tables DEEP-merge: a pointed file setting only `frontier.model`, over a
      discovered config carrying `frontier.provider` AND a `frontier.fallback` chain, yields the
      overridden model AND the discovered provider AND the discovered fallback chain. This is the
      criterion that fails against `dict.update` semantics — the existing shallow merge drops both
      siblings, so the test is not satisfiable by the current machinery and cannot pass vacuously.
- [ ] a test asserts ARRAYS REPLACE rather than append: a `fallback` chain in the pointed file yields
      EXACTLY that chain (not the concatenation with the discovered one), and `fallback = []` yields
      no fallbacks at all — the "CI pins fail-loudly over a project default" case.
- [ ] a test asserts `read_reserved_section`'s own SHALLOW-merge behaviour is UNCHANGED for a non-llm
      reserved section, proving the deep merge did not leak into shared config machinery. The parent
      plan forbids editing that helper; this criterion is what detects the mis-scope.

## Read the env var as a STRING LITERAL (the doc-gate footgun)

`REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` MUST be read as a literal:

    os.environ.get("REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE")

NOT via a variable, an f-string, or any other indirection. `docs/env-vars.md` is DERIVED by
`scripts/gen_env_registry.py`, a STATIC AST scanner that only records names appearing as string
LITERALS in an `os.environ.get(...)` call, and CI has a drift gate that regenerates the file and
fails the build when the committed copy differs.

An indirect read passes every runtime test while the scanner files it under "name not statically
determinable" and the variable never gets documented — a green test suite and a broken doc gate.

This is not hypothetical: it happened on sibling task f844 in this same epic. The nine
`REBAR_LLM_{FRONTIER,STANDARD,TRIVIAL}_{MODEL,PROVIDER,ENDPOINT}` vars were first built with an
f-string, 16/16 behavioural tests passed, six mutations were caught, and the change would still
have failed CI. See the literal-read pattern and its explanatory comment in
`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py` (`_ENV_VAR_NAMES` + `_env_override`) and copy it.

## Merge semantics (decided on the parent, eb58 — do not re-derive)

Deep/recursive over tables (leaf key wins); arrays replaced wholesale, never appended. Precedence:
CLI `-c` > env > `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` > discovered file > default. Secrets stay env-only.

**Do NOT change `read_reserved_section`** (`config.py:588-600`). Its `merged.update(sub)` is shared by
every reserved section; deepening it would silently alter layering for unrelated consumers. Implement
the deep merge in the llm resolver over the section dict it receives. Editing that helper means the
change is mis-scoped.
